# GMX Open Interest Alarm App — Product & Technical Spec

**Status:** Draft v2 for team review **Prepared:** Jul 30, 2026 **Owner:** \[add name\] **Audience:** Product/eng review → handoff to AI dev agents

### Changelog (v1 → v2)

- MVP architecture locked to **on-device polling only** (backend push moved to post-MVP roadmap)  
- Multiple simultaneous alarms (same or different tokens) explicitly confirmed as core behavior

---

## 1\. Purpose

Let a user set one or more alarms on **GMX Long Open Interest %** for a chosen token, and get notified when it crosses a threshold in a chosen direction (up or down). This is a positioning/sentiment signal — traders use long/short OI skew as a contrarian or momentum indicator.

**A user can create multiple alarms, on the same token or different tokens, simultaneously.** For example: "BTC-USD cross up 55%" and "BTC-USD cross down 45%" as two independent, coexisting alarms on the same market (this was the original motivating example) — plus any number of alarms on other tokens (ETH-USD, SOL-USD, etc.). There's no assumed limit in this spec; if the team wants a cap for MVP (e.g. 20 active alarms), add it as a config constant.

**v1 / MVP scope:** Android app, Arbitrum chain only, on-device polling, no accounts/backend, hardcoded token list.

---

## 2\. Core Metric

longPct  \= longInterestUsd  / (longInterestUsd \+ shortInterestUsd) \* 100

shortPct \= 100 \- longPct

Matches the "52% / 48%" split shown in GMX's own UI. Source data from GMX's public API (§6).

## 3\. App Navigation / Screens

### 3.1 Home screen (on open)

The first thing the user sees. Shows:

- **Connection/data status indicator** — e.g. `🟢 Connected · updated 12s ago` or `🔴 Connection issue · retrying`. This should reflect the on-device polling loop's actual health (last successful fetch timestamp), not just device network state.  
- **Two primary actions (buttons):**  
  - `+ Create Alarm`  
  - `View Alarms` (shows a count badge, e.g. "4 active · 1 triggered")

### 3.2 Create/Edit Alarm screen

The form described in §4, plus a **live preview** of the selected token's current longPct (confirmed good — keep this).

### 3.3 Alarms List screen

One scrollable list of all alarms, color-coded by state (§5.3). Tapping an alarm opens its detail view, which includes that alarm's own trigger history — so trigger history doesn't need to be a separate top-level tab, it's nested per-alarm. (If the team later wants a single global feed of "everything that fired recently across all alarms," that's a cheap addition on top of this same data model — flagged as an easy v1.1 add, not required for MVP.)

Home

 ├── Create Alarm  →  (on save) → Alarms List

 └── View Alarms   →  Alarms List

                        └── tap an alarm → Alarm Detail (edit fields \+ its trigger history)

## 5\. Alarm Evaluation Logic

**Must be edge-triggered**, not level-triggered — otherwise a "cross up 55" alarm fires on *every poll* for as long as the value stays above 55%, instead of once at the moment it crosses.

function evaluate(alarm, currentPct):

    if alarm.lastSeenPct is null:

        alarm.lastSeenPct \= currentPct

        return   \# first read just establishes a baseline, never fires

    crossedUp   \= alarm.lastSeenPct \<  alarm.threshold \<= currentPct

    crossedDown \= alarm.lastSeenPct \>  alarm.threshold \>= currentPct

    if alarm.armed:

        if (alarm.direction \== UP   and crossedUp) or

           (alarm.direction \== DOWN and crossedDown):

            fire(alarm, currentPct)

            alarm.lastTriggeredAt \= now()

            alarm.acknowledged \= false      \# drives the "triggered" color in the list

            alarm.armed \= false             \# always disarms on fire

    if not alarm.armed and alarm.triggerMode \== REPEATING:

        if alarm.direction \== UP and currentPct \< (alarm.threshold \- alarm.hysteresisBuffer):

            alarm.armed \= true              \# silently re-arms, no notification

        elif alarm.direction \== DOWN and currentPct \> (alarm.threshold \+ alarm.hysteresisBuffer):

            alarm.armed \= true

    alarm.lastSeenPct \= currentPct

    \# Note: one-time alarms simply never re-arm — alarm.enabled stays true,

    \# but alarm.armed stays false until the user manually re-enables it.

### 5.1 Why hysteresis matters

Without the re-arm buffer, a repeating alarm at threshold 55% would fire again and again while longPct oscillates between, say, 54.9% and 55.1% every poll — one real event, dozens of duplicate notifications. The buffer means: after firing, the value has to retreat a bit before the alarm is willing to fire again.

### 5.2 Worked example

Alarm: `BTC-USD`, direction \= **Up**, threshold \= **55%**, mode \= **Repeating**, hysteresis buffer \= **2%**, polling \= 15s.

| Poll | longPct | Armed (before) | Crossed? | Action | Armed (after) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| t0 | 52% | *(baseline)* | — | none — just sets lastSeenPct | true |
| t1 | 54% | true | no (54 \< 55\) | none | true |
| t2 | 56% | true | **yes** (54 → 56 passes through 55\) | 🔔 **Fires**: "crossed up 55%, now 56%" | **false** |
| t3 | 57% | false | n/a, not armed | none — no duplicate notification | false |
| t4 | 55.5% | false | n/a | none | false |
| t5 | 53% | false | check re-arm: 53 \< (55−2)=53 → not yet (needs to go *below* 53\) | none | false |
| t6 | 52% | false | 52 \< 53 → re-arm condition met | silently re-arms, **no notification** | **true** |
| t7 | 56% | true | **yes** (52→56 passes 55\) | 🔔 **Fires again**: "crossed up 55%, now 56%" | false |

Takeaways:

- It fires exactly once per genuine crossing, not once per poll.  
- Between t2 and t6, longPct stayed above the threshold most of the time — correctly silent.  
- The alarm only becomes fireable again after retreating past 53% (55 − 2 buffer), which is what stops "hovering near 55%" from re-triggering it constantly.  
- **One-time mode** would behave identically through t2, then simply never re-arm (t6 wouldn't flip `armed` back to true) — the user would have to manually re-enable it.

## 6\. API Integration

### 6.1 Endpoint

GET https://arbitrum.gmxapi.io/v1/pairs

GET https://arbitrum.gmxapi.ai/v1/pairs   ← identical peer host, use as fallback

Public, no auth. One call returns every GMX Arbitrum market in one response.

### 6.2 Fields used

{

  "ticker\_id": "BTC\_USD",

  "base\_currency": "BTC",

  "last\_price": 64028.52,

  "volume\_usd": 13800000,

  "long\_open\_interest": 6900000,

  "short\_open\_interest": 6400000

}

longPct \= long\_open\_interest / (long\_open\_interest \+ short\_open\_interest) \* 100

Worked check: `6.9m / (6.9m + 6.4m) = 51.9% ≈ 52%` — matches the GMX UI screenshot this project started from. ✓

> ⚠️ `long_open_interest` / `short_open_interest` can be **missing/null** on spot-only pools. Filter those out — don't show them in the token list and don't evaluate alarms against them.

### 6.3 Token list: **hardcoded for MVP**

Per your note — skip live API-driven ranking for now. Process:

1. During development, call `/pairs` **once manually**, sort by `volume_usd` descending, and hand-pick the top \~30 entries with non-null OI fields.  
2. Paste that into a static JSON/array bundled with the app (symbol, display name, `ticker_id`).  
3. GMX's Arbitrum deployment currently lists on the order of 30+ actively-traded perp markets (per third-party trackers), so a top-30 cut is a reasonable target — but **confirm the exact live count and composition from `/pairs` yourselves** rather than trusting a list here, since the token roster changes over time and I can't independently verify current values against live data from this environment.  
4. Flag as a clear v2 item: swap the hardcoded list for a periodic (e.g. every 15 min) live refresh from `/pairs` sorted by volume — the evaluation logic doesn't change at all, only where the dropdown's options come from.

### 6.4 Polling frequency

No published rate limit found in GMX's docs for this endpoint, and it returns all markets in one call so cost doesn't scale with number of alarms.

**Recommendation:** presets of 15s / 30s / 1 min / 5 min, **default and floor at 15s** (matches your requested default). Exponential backoff on `429`/`5xx`; fail over to the `.ai` peer host on error; skip the poll cycle rather than firing on missing/stale data.

## 7\. Architecture — MVP: on-device polling

Locking this in as the MVP approach per your direction. Worth documenting the real constraint so it doesn't surprise anyone mid-build:

- Android restricts background execution (Doze / App Standby). Plain `WorkManager` periodic work has a **15-minute minimum interval** — it cannot do 15-second polling in the background.  
- To actually hit a 15s cadence, the app needs a **foreground service**: a long-running service with a persistent (low-priority) notification — e.g. *"Watching 4 GMX alarms"* — that runs the polling loop while alive. This requires the `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` permission (and on Android 14+, a declared foreground service type — `dataSync` is the closest fit).  
- Recommend prompting the user once to exclude the app from battery optimization (`REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS`), since some OEMs (Xiaomi, Huawei, etc.) kill foreground services aggressively regardless of the standard Android APIs.  
- **Known MVP limitation, worth stating plainly to the team and eventually the user:** if the OS or an aggressive OEM battery manager kills the service, alarms silently stop evaluating until the app is reopened. There's no way to fully eliminate this risk with on-device-only polling — the persistent notification actually doubles as a rough "is this still running" signal for the user.  
- This limitation is exactly what a backend-push model (poll server-side, notify via FCM) removes entirely — kept in the v2 roadmap (§10) as the natural next step once MVP validates the concept.

flowchart LR

    A\[Foreground service\<br/\>timer loop, every 15s\] \--\> B\[GET /pairs\<br/\>arbitrum.gmxapi.io\]

    B \--\> C\[Compute longPct\<br/\>per market\]

    C \--\> D{Evaluate against\<br/\>all local alarms}

    D \--\>|crossing detected| E\[Local notification\<br/\>+ mark alarm 'triggered'\]

    D \--\>|no crossing| F\[Update lastSeenPct,\<br/\>wait next cycle\]

## 8\. Alarm state & list-screen colors

Three states, each with a distinct visual treatment in the Alarms List:

| State | When | List appearance |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Active / Armed** | Enabled, evaluating normally, hasn't fired since last acknowledgment | Normal card styling |
| **Triggered** | Has fired and not yet acknowledged (`lastTriggeredAt` set, `acknowledged = false`) | Highlighted color (e.g. amber/red accent or badge) — this is the state you flagged as needing visual identification |
| **Disabled/Paused** | `enabled = false` | Greyed out / muted |

**Clearing the "triggered" highlight:** opening the alarm's detail view sets `acknowledged = true`, returning it to normal Active styling (same pattern as an unread-message inbox — familiar, no new UX to design). This is simpler than a time-based auto-clear and keeps the state fully user-controlled.

| :---- | :---- |

| alarmId | UUID (FK) |

## 10\. Non-functional requirements

- **Notification permission:** Android 13+ requires runtime `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` — request during onboarding.  
- **Foreground service permission/type:** required for the polling loop to survive backgrounding (§7).  
- **Offline/error handling:** on fetch failure, don't evaluate that cycle — surface a status change on the Home screen indicator rather than guessing at stale data.  
- **No sensitive data:** `/pairs` is public/read-only; no wallet or auth data involved in this feature.

2. GMX lists multiple isolated pools per index token (e.g. different collateral variants of BTC/USD). Show each separately in the token dropdown, or aggregate? Recommend: show separately for MVP (simplest, matches the source data 1:1).  
3. Any hard cap on number of simultaneous alarms per user for MVP, given everything runs on-device?  
4. Acceptable to ship knowing the foreground service can be killed by aggressive OEM battery managers (§7), with the persistent notification as the only user-facing signal of that risk for MVP?

## 12\. Suggested phasing

- **MVP (this doc):** On-device foreground-service polling, Arbitrum only, hardcoded top-30 token list, local notifications, per-alarm trigger history.  
- **v2:** Migrate to backend poller \+ push notifications (removes the OEM-kill risk entirely, see §7); make token list dynamic via live `/pairs` ranking; multi-chain (Avalanche etc.); absolute-USD OI thresholds in addition to %.

**Calculator of OI Percentage, for 1 asset with ‘TARGET\_MARKET’:**

*import requests*  
*from decimal import Decimal*

*API\_URL \= "https://arbitrum-api.gmxinfra.io/markets/info"*  
*TARGET\_MARKET \= "0x09400D9DB990D5ed3f35D7be61DfAEB900Af03C9".lower()*

*data \= requests.get(API\_URL, timeout=20).json()*

*\# API response is normally: {"markets": \[...\]}*  
*markets \= data\["markets"\] if isinstance(data, dict) else data*

*market \= next(*  
    *(*  
        *m for m in markets*  
        *if m.get("marketToken", "").lower() \== TARGET\_MARKET*  
    *),*  
    *None,*  
*)*

*if market is None:*  
    *raise RuntimeError("SOL/USD \[SOL-USDC\] market not found")*

*long\_oi \= Decimal(market\["openInterestLong"\])*  
*short\_oi \= Decimal(market\["openInterestShort"\])*  
*total\_oi \= long\_oi \+ short\_oi*

*long\_pct \= long\_oi / total\_oi \* Decimal("100")*  
*short\_pct \= short\_oi / total\_oi \* Decimal("100")*

*print("Market:", market\["name"\])*  
*print("Market token:", market\["marketToken"\])*  
*print("Index token:", market\["indexToken"\])*  
*print("Long token:", market\["longToken"\])*  
*print("Short token:", market\["shortToken"\])*  
*print()*  
*print("Long OI:", long\_oi / Decimal(10\*\*30))*  
*print("Short OI:", short\_oi / Decimal(10\*\*30))*  
*print("Long percentage:", round(long\_pct, 2), "%")*  
*print("Short percentage:", round(short\_pct, 2), "%")*

**List all Tokens OI:**  
*import requests*  
*from decimal import Decimal*

*API\_URL \= "https://arbitrum-api.gmxinfra.io/markets/info"*  
*USD\_DECIMALS \= Decimal(10) \*\* 30*

*response \= requests.get(API\_URL, timeout=20)*  
*response.raise\_for\_status()*

*data \= response.json()*  
*markets \= data.get("markets", data)*

*results \= \[\]*

*for market in markets:*  
    *try:*  
        *long\_oi\_raw \= Decimal(str(market.get("openInterestLong", 0)))*  
        *short\_oi\_raw \= Decimal(str(market.get("openInterestShort", 0)))*

        *total\_oi\_raw \= long\_oi\_raw \+ short\_oi\_raw*

        *if total\_oi\_raw \== 0:*  
            *long\_percent \= Decimal("50")*  
            *short\_percent \= Decimal("50")*  
        *else:*  
            *long\_percent \= (*  
                *long\_oi\_raw / total\_oi\_raw \* Decimal("100")*  
            *)*  
            *short\_percent \= (*  
                *short\_oi\_raw / total\_oi\_raw \* Decimal("100")*  
            *)*

        *results.append({*  
            *"name": market.get("name"),*  
            *"marketToken": market.get("marketToken"),*  
            *"indexToken": market.get("indexToken"),*  
            *"longToken": market.get("longToken"),*  
            *"shortToken": market.get("shortToken"),*

            *\# Human-readable USD values*  
            *"longOI": long\_oi\_raw / USD\_DECIMALS,*  
            *"shortOI": short\_oi\_raw / USD\_DECIMALS,*  
            *"totalOI": total\_oi\_raw / USD\_DECIMALS,*

            *\# Exact calculated percentages*  
            *"longPercent": long\_percent,*  
            *"shortPercent": short\_percent,*  
        *})*

    *except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, ArithmeticError):*  
        *print("Skipped invalid market:", market.get("name"))*

    *\# Sort the results list by the 'name' key alphabetically*  
    *sorted\_results \= sorted(results, key=lambda x: x\['name'\])*  
    *with open("GMX-List.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:*  
        *for item in sorted\_results:*  
            *f.write(f"{item\['name'\]} \- Long: {item\['longPercent'\]:.2f}% | Short: {item\['shortPercent'\]:.2f}%\\n")*

        *\# print(f"{item\['name'\]} \- Long: {item\['longPercent'\]:.2f}% | Short: {item\['shortPercent'\]:.2f}%")*

        *\# print(f"\\n{item\['name'\]}")*  
        *\# \# print("-" \* len(item\["name"\]))*

        *\# \# print("Market token:", item\["marketToken"\])*  
        *\# \# print("Index token: ", item\["indexToken"\])*  
        *\# \# print("Long token:  ", item\["longToken"\])*  
        *\# \# print("Short token: ", item\["shortToken"\])*

        *\# \# print(f"Long OI:     ${item\['longOI'\]:,.2f}")*  
        *\# \# print(f"Short OI:    ${item\['shortOI'\]:,.2f}")*  
        *\# \# print(f"Total OI:    ${item\['totalOI'\]:,.2f}")*

        *\# print(f"Long:        {item\['longPercent'\]:.2f}%")*  
        *\# print(f"Short:       {item\['shortPercent'\]:.2f}%")*
